name: Question 5
worked_solution:
We note that $12{x}^{5}$ is the derivative of the quantity in the square root. So we make a substitution

$$
u=2{x}^{6}-3.
$$

Its derivative is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} & =12{x}^{5}\,⟹\,\text{d}u=12{x}^{5}\,\text{d}x,\end{aligned}
$$

and rewriting our integral, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 12{x}^{5}\sqrt{2{x}^{6}-3}\,\text{d}x & =\int \sqrt{2{x}^{6}-3}\cdot 12{x}^{5}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int \sqrt{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\int {u}^{1/2}\,\text{d}u.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now solve the integral using the power rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {u}^{1/2}\,\text{d}u & =\frac{{u}^{3/2}}{(\frac{3}{2})}+C \\  & =\frac{2{u}^{3/2}}{3}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Lastly, we substitute $u=2{x}^{6}-3$ back in the expression. So the final result is

$$
\int 12{x}^{5}\sqrt{2{x}^{6}-3}\,\text{d}x=\frac{2(2{x}^{6}-3)^{3/2}}{3}+C.
$$

Question 5
?

Calculate ∫12x52x6−3dx.

a
2(2x6−3)3/23+C
b
−122x6−3+C
c
−22x6−3+C
d
3(2x6−3)3/22+C
e
(2x6−3)3/22+C
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We note that 12x5 is the derivative of the quantity in the square root. So we make a substitution u=2x6−3. Its derivative is given by

dudx=12x5⟹du=12x5dx,

and rewriting our integral, we get ∫12x52x6−3dx=∫2x6−3⋅12x5dx=∫udu=∫u1/2du.

We can now solve the integral using the power rule: ∫u1/2du=u3/2(32)+C=2u3/23+C

Lastly, we substitute u=2x6−3 back in the expression. So the final result is ∫12x52x6−3dx=2(2x6−3)3/23+C.
